Repo: /Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/expnese-tracker-attempts/yfl-expense-tracker-svelte-generated

TASK: Update `docs/product-backlog.md` — this is the single working backlog (one maintainer; one-liner items). Read it first to match its exact section structure, heading style, and one-liner format. Add the following as concise one-liners under the most appropriate existing sections (create a subsection only if the file's style clearly calls for it). Do not duplicate items already present.

ADD these dangling-capability / reconciliation items:
1. **Unmatched-expenses filter never finished**: `Expense.matched_transaction_id` is selected and populated (and unit-tested) but no Expenses-page UI consumes it — the "Hide Matched" toggle was specced (umf1a/2a/3a) but never built. Decide: build the toggle or drop the field.
2. **Reconcile stale backlog item**: "Shrink large uploads" is listed as an unbuilt Feature but is already implemented and wired (client-side Canvas resize in `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate`). Remove/mark it done.

ADD these optional test-coverage follow-ups (as a small "test-coverage backlog" group of one-liners — low priority, engineering):
3. Extract + unit-test the Expenses-page CSV export FILENAME branching (`expenses_<from>_to_<to>.csv` etc.), currently inline and untested in `src/routes/expenses/+page.svelte`.
4. Add direct unit tests for `getSignedReceiptUrl()` null/empty-path → null (no API call) and storage-error → null (no throw); and assert the 300s OCR signed-URL expiry value. Only the batch variant `collectSignedUrls` is currently tested.
5. Add PDF-export assertions for US-Letter page dimensions (612×792) and per-category row-number restart at 1 (`PDFExportService`), currently unasserted.
6. Resend webhook handler orchestration (process-all-attachments loop, body-text fallback — eaf4a/eaf5a) remains unit-untestable until the handler is refactored to be importable; already tracked in `docs/prd-resend-handler-testability.md` — cross-reference it.

Also note (one-liner, low priority) the deferred/aspirational items surfaced during the spec audit, ONLY if the backlog is the right home for them:
7. Recent-categories dropdown section (exp2b), mobile-responsive category dropdown (exp8a), and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support (exp8b) were specced but never implemented — capture as optional UX enhancements.
8. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (vca2a email path) and read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal (fcr2b) were specced but not implemented.

Keep each to one line, in the file's voice. Do NOT `git commit`. Do NOT run repo-wide prettier; if needed, `npx prettier --write docs/product-backlog.md` only.

Report the exact lines you added and under which sections.

A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. - verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Backlog
2	
3	The single working list — features, UX bugs, engineering, open questions, and
4	refactoring. Refactoring items are summarized here as one-liners; the full
5	detail (smell, effort, sibling sites, plan) lives in
6	[Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md), which is a reference, not a
7	separate to-do list.
8	
9	## Features
10	
11	- **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
12	- **Shrink large uploads.** When an image is too large on upload, shrink it. Maybe always do this.
13	- **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account.
14	- **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it.
15	- **iPhone camera.** Use the Camera app on iPhone to take photos of receipts.
16	
17	## Bugs / UX issues
18	
19	- **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
20	- **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
21	- **Blank transaction date hint.** When the transaction date is blank, show the expected date format for someone who is typing.
22	
23	## Engineering
24	
25	- **Test the Resend webhook handler.** Extract `handleResendWebhook(req, deps)` from `Deno.serve` and inject its collaborators so the branch matrix (auth gates, body/attachment flow, notify-on-failure) is unit-testable in vitest. See [PRD — Make the Resend webhook handler testable](prd-resend-handler-testability.md).
26	
27	## Refactoring
28	
29	Open items only — full detail in [Refactoring backlog](refactoring-backlog.md).
30	(RF-01–03 are done; RF-D1/D2 are deferred pending a decision.)
31	
32	- **[RF-04](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-04--findpotentialmatches-vs-findpotentialmatchesfortransaction-are-a-copy-paste-pair)** — De-duplicate the `findPotentialMatches` / `findPotentialMatchesForTransaction` copy-paste pair.
33	- **[RF-05](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-05--long-methods-in-the-service-layer)** — Break up the long methods in the service layer.
34	- **[RF-06](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-06--matching-tolerances-are-a-long-parameter-list--data-clump)** — Bundle the matching tolerances (Long Parameter List / Data Clump) into one object _(correctness-adjacent)_.
35	- **[RF-07](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-07--singleton-vs-dependency-injection-split-across-services)** — Reconcile the singleton-vs-dependency-injection split across services.
36	- **[RF-08](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-08--any-where-a-precise-type-exists)** — Replace `any` with precise types where one already exists.
37	- **[RF-09](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-09--three-inconsistent-ways-to-resolve-a-rows-category)** — Collapse the three inconsistent ways to resolve a row's Category into one.
38	- **[RF-10](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-10--reconciliationservice-does-ui-display-massaging)** — Move UI display massaging out of `ReconciliationService` (Feature Envy).
39	- **[RF-11](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-11--normalizeamountinvertsign-boolean-flag-argument)** — Replace the `normalizeAmount(invertSign: boolean)` flag argument.
40	- **[RF-12](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-12--magic-number-matching-defaults)** — Name the magic-number matching defaults.
41	- **[RF-13](refactoring-backlog.md#rf-13--pdfexportserviceshouldenablepdfexport-static--state-object)** — Fix `PDFExportService.shouldEnablePDFExport` (Inappropriate Static + state object).
42	
43	## Open questions
44	
45	- **Combining receipts for one expense.** How to handle when two receipts should be combined into one expense to match — e.g. two medications picked up at the same time.
46	- **WealthSimple refund handling.** WealthSimple records several rows when a refund is issued. Example:
47	
48	  ```csv
49	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-24","Refund initiated","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
50	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","33.9","CAD"
51	  "2026-05-24","2026-05-25","Refund settled","MARSHES GOLF CORPORATI","-33.9","CAD"
52	  ```
